rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages of human creation culminating in a new creation make resurrection plainly possible, so it needs little further emphasis.
rows.anchor: أكبر دليل على أن إعادته ممكنة ليس في ذلك أدنى ريب، فلا يحتاج بعد هذه الأدلة إلى كبير توكيد

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī explains that prior description of human creation through wondrous stages already establishes God's wisdom and power, so resurrection needs less emphasis than death.
rows.anchor: جاء في (روح المعاني) : "ولم يؤكد سبحانه أمرَ البعث تأكيده لأمر الموت مع كثرة

rows.speaker: البحر المحيط
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ says resurrection is stated as an established certainty with only inna, so a second emphasis is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: جاء في (البحر المحيط) : "ولم تؤكد جملة البعث إلا بإن لأنه أبرز في سورة المقطوع به الذي لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In human reasoning, re-creating what was first made is easier than originating it: the first creation receives lām and qad, while resurrection receives only inna; for God, nothing is easier than anything else.
rows.anchor: إن الإعادة أسهل من الابتداء في منطق العقل، فإن الذي يصنع كل يوم آلاف النماذج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The perfected, wondrous creation can suggest that humanity was made to endure, making the announcement of death after all that seem unexpected and warranting its emphasis.
rows.anchor: إن ما ذكره الله من خلق الإنسانه وتطويره حتى صار مخلوقاً على أحسن هيئة

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī says the preceding stress on God's precise creation makes death so counterintuitive that an unobservant listener might almost deny it, explaining the extra emphasis on mortality.
rows.anchor: جاء في (روح المعاني) : "ولما تضمنت الجملة السابقة المبالغة في أنه تعالى شأنه أحكم خلق الإنسان وأتقنه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People often forget death amid worldly concerns and behave as if it will not come; the reminders in al-Takāthur and al-Shuʿarāʾ illustrate this heedlessness.
rows.anchor: إن الإنسان كثيراً ما يغفل عن الموت فينشغل بالحياة وتلهيه أمورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death receives doubled emphasis in al-Muʾminūn because the sūra repeatedly depicts death and mortality, whereas al-Zumar mentions death only twice.
rows.anchor: لقد أكد الموت في آية (المؤمنون) بإن واللام في حين أكده في الزمر بإن وحدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author flags a further ending contrast for explanation: al-Muʾminūn concludes this sequence with death, while al-Zumar concludes with disputation before their Lord.
rows.anchor: لِمَ ختم آية (المؤمنون) بالبعث فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author undertakes a comparison of the parallel Musa narratives because their broad similarity leaves meaningful wording differences to explain, including jāʾahā versus atāhā and adkhil versus usluk.
rows.anchor: بينهما تشابهاً كبيراً ولا يتبيّن سِرُّ الاختلاف في التعبير بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Naml account says Musa perceived a fire; al-Qaṣaṣ adds that it was from the side of the mountain.
rows.anchor: النمل القصص {إني آنَسْتُ نَاراً} {آنَسَ مِن جَانِبِ الطور نَاراً}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds Musa's instruction for his family to stay while he goes to the fire; the comparison lists this detail as absent from Naml.
rows.anchor: - {امكثوا} {سَآتِيكُمْ مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ} {لعلي آتِيكُمْ مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml uses a definite promise that Musa will bring news, while al-Qaṣaṣ phrases it as a hope or possibility.
rows.anchor: {سَآتِيكُمْ مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ} {لعلي آتِيكُمْ مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Naml wording specifies a burning brand, while al-Qaṣaṣ speaks more generally of a firebrand.
rows.anchor: {أَوْ آتِيكُمْ بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ} {أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ النار}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel accounts differ between jāʾahā in Naml and atāhā in al-Qaṣaṣ.
rows.anchor: {فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا} {فَلَمَّآ أَتَاهَا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml reports the blessing spoken at the call; al-Qaṣaṣ instead specifies the place from which the call came.
rows.anchor: {نُودِيَ أَن بُورِكَ} {نُودِيَ مِن شَاطِىءِ الوادي الأيمن}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Naml account includes a glorification of God at the call that is absent from al-Qaṣaṣ.
rows.anchor: {وَسُبْحَانَ الله رَبِّ العالمين} -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml directly addresses Musa, while al-Qaṣaṣ introduces the address with explanatory an.
rows.anchor: {ياموسى} {أَن ياموسى} {إِنَّهُ أَنَا الله العزيز الحكيم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml uses the pronoun of شأن and the names al-ʿAzīz and al-Ḥakīm, whereas al-Qaṣaṣ identifies God as Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: {إِنَّهُ أَنَا الله العزيز الحكيم} {إني أَنَا الله رَبُّ العالمين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml gives the command to throw the staff directly; al-Qaṣaṣ prefixes it with wa-an.
rows.anchor: {وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ} {وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds a command to come forward before saying not to fear; Naml has only the shorter reassurance.
rows.anchor: {ياموسى لاَ تَخَفْ} {ياموسى أَقْبِلْ وَلاَ تَخَفْ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml says messengers do not fear in God's presence; al-Qaṣaṣ directly assures Musa that he is among the safe.
rows.anchor: {إِنِّي لاَ يَخَافُ لَدَيَّ المرسلون} {إِنَّكَ مِنَ الآمنين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml adds an exception for one who sinned and then replaced evil with good; the author lists no parallel exception in al-Qaṣaṣ.
rows.anchor: {إِلاَّ مَن ظَلَمَ} {وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ} {اسلك يَدَكَ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Naml account says adkhil and al-Qaṣaṣ says usluk for putting the hand into the bosom.
rows.anchor: {وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ} {اسلك يَدَكَ}

words: أَنۢ بُورِكَ مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml alone includes the blessing over those in and around the fire and God's glorification, fitting its scene of exaltation; the utterance honors the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: الموقف في النمل موقفُ تعظيمٍ كما أسلفنا وهذا القول تعظيم لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct call in Naml honors Musa, while explanatory an in al-Qaṣaṣ conveys an address to this effect rather than necessarily its exact wording; the author compares the call to Ibrahim with God's direct speech to Noah.
rows.anchor: فَشرَّفه بالنداء المباشر في حين ليس المقام كذلك في القصص، فجاء بما يفسر الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expanded, detailed mode of al-Qaṣaṣ also suits its extra explanatory particle an.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن المقام في سورة القصص، مقام تبسّط وتفصيل فجاء بـ (أن) زيادة في التبسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greater burden of Musa's assignment in Naml calls for direct address; the mode of address varies with the task and its weight.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن ثقل التكليف في النمل يستدعي المباشرة في النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml uses the pronoun of شأن in inna-hu ana as an expression of grandeur, while al-Qaṣaṣ omits it.
rows.anchor: فجاء بضمير الشأن الدال على التعظيم في آية النمل: {إِنَّهُ أَنَا} ولم يأت به في القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml's added divine names al-ʿAzīz and al-Ḥakīm heighten the scene's grandeur.
rows.anchor: ثم جاء باسميه الكريمين: {العزيز الحكيم} في النمل زيادة في التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour's arrival in the afterlife for deniers is the harder, more grievous scene and takes jāʾa; the worldly appeal, where God may lift what is invoked, takes atā.
rows.anchor: فالموقف الأول أشق وأشد مما في الثانية، فجاء بالفعل (جاء) لما هو أصعب وأشق. ويستعمل (أتى) لما هو أخف وأيسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues that jāʾa is morphologically heavier: the Qur'an uses only its past form, whereas atā occurs in past, present, imperative, and participial forms, matching heavier and lighter scenes.
rows.anchor: الفعل (جاء) أثقل من (أتى) في اللفظ بدليل أنه لم يرد في القرآن فعل مضارع لـ (جاء)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to the Musa narratives, the author notes that Naml uses jāʾahā and al-Qaṣaṣ uses atāhā, applying the heavier-versus-lighter contrast to their wording.
rows.anchor: ونعود إلى ما نحن فيه من قصة موسى، فقد قال في سورة النمل: {فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا} وقال في سورة القصص: {فَلَمَّآ أَتَاهَا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: S-l-k evokes threading something through an opening; idkhāl is more specific and more laborious, while sulūk can be easy, as the bee's paths and water's channels illustrate.
rows.anchor: سلكت الخيط في المخيط، أي: أدخلته فيه. فالإدخالُ أَخصُّ وأشقُّ من السلك والسلوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harder idkhāl suits Naml's firm promise, arrival, and difficult mission to Pharaoh; the easier sulūk suits the fearful setting of al-Qaṣaṣ, while idkhāl fits security and trust.
rows.anchor: وناسب أن يوضع السلوك في مقام الخوف، وأن يوضع الإدخال في مقام الأمن والثقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more specific idkhāl pairs with the more specific shihāb qabas, while the broader sulūk pairs with the broader jadwah.
rows.anchor: وناسب أن يوضع الإدخال، وهو أخص من السلوك مع (الشهاب القبس) الذي هو أخَصُّ من الجذوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-rahab means fear; al-Qaṣaṣ includes the wing gesture because fear recurs throughout its story and its telling is more detailed, unlike Naml.
rows.anchor: و (الرهب) هو الخوف، وهو مناسبٌ لجو الخوف الذي تردد في القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml gives Musa nine signs in a scene of confidence and strength, broadening the mission; al-Qaṣaṣ names two proofs in its different setting.
rows.anchor: فقد أعطاه في النمل تسع آيات إلى فرعون، وذكر في القصص برهانين، وذلك لما كان المقام في النمل مقامَ ثِقةٍ وقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds aqbil because its detailed telling allows fuller speech and Musa's pervasive fear suggests he fled farther, so he must be called back as well as reassured.
rows.anchor: مقام الإيجاز في النمل يستدعي عدم الإطالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recurrent atmosphere of fear in al-Qaṣaṣ indicates Musa had fled far, prompting the additional call to come forward.
rows.anchor: أن شيوع جو الخوف في القصص يدل على إيغال موسى في الهرب، فدعاه إلى الإقبال وعدم الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ assures a frightened Musa that he is safe; Naml's statement about messengers not fearing in God's presence honors him by hinting he belongs among them.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن المقام في سورة القصص مقام الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml's ladayya suggests closeness; its direct ya-Musa and alqi, without explanatory particles, likewise signal proximity between God and Musa.
rows.anchor: ثم انظر كيف قال: {لَدَيَّ} مُشْعِراً بالقُربِ وهو زيادةٌ في التكريم والتشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā yakhāfu ladayya means messengers feel no fear in God's presence, not that they fear nothing of Him; the Prophet's statement that he is most God-fearing supports their reverence.
rows.anchor: لأن المرسلين لا يخافون بحضرته، ولكنهم يخشونه ويخافونه كل الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml's exception for a wrongdoer who reforms is omitted in al-Qaṣaṣ because qualifying the direct assurance that Musa is among the safe would sound incoherent.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يحسن أن يقال: (إنك من الآمنين إلا من ظلم، ثم بدل حسناً بعد سوء..) ولو قال هذا لم يكن كلاماً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reform exception fits the Queen of Sheba, who left sun-worship and submitted to God; Moses was already a believer, and his confession of wrong concerned killing the Egyptian, not a change from disbelief.
rows.anchor: فإنها ظلمت نفسها بكفرها وسجودِها للشمس من دون الله، ثم بدّلت حُسْناً بعد سوء، فأسلمتْ لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Naml account says nine signs, while al-Qaṣaṣ calls the two hand and staff signs two proofs.
rows.anchor: {فِي تِسْعِ آيَاتٍ} {فَذَانِكَ بُرْهَانَانِ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wing gesture from fear occurs in al-Qaṣaṣ but not Naml.
rows.anchor: - {واضمم إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ الرهب} {إلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml describes the mission as going to Pharaoh and his people; al-Qaṣaṣ names Pharaoh and his chiefs.
rows.anchor: {إلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِ} {إلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ tells Musa's story at length from before his birth through the drowning of Pharaoh, while Naml gives a brief summary; the differing expressions suit each account's scale.
rows.anchor: فالقصة في سورة القصص، إذن مفصلة مطولة، وفي سورة النمل مُوجَزة مجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear frames al-Qaṣaṣ from Musa's mother's alarm to Musa's fear after killing the Egyptian and his fearful flight from the city, while Naml mentions fear only at the staff miracle.
rows.anchor: في سورة القصص، كان جو القصة مطبوعاً بطابع الخوف الذي يسيطر على موسى، عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear continues in al-Qaṣaṣ as Musa prays for rescue, receives reassurance in Midian, fears Pharaoh's killing and denial, and asks Aaron to assist him; this contrasts with Naml's brief, less fearful story.
rows.anchor: وهذا الطابع - أعني طابع الخوف - يبقى ملازماً للقصة إلى أواخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds the location on the mountain's side because that sūra develops the scene in greater detail.
rows.anchor: فزاد {مِن جَانِبِ الطور} وذلك لمقامِ التفصيلِ الذي بُنيت عليه القصة في سورة القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds Musa's instruction to his family to stay, another detail suited to its expanded narrative rather than Naml's concise account.
rows.anchor: بزيادة {امكثوا} . وهذه الزيادة نظيرة ما ذكرناه آنفاً أعني مناسبة لمقامِ التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa's fear in al-Qaṣaṣ makes his promise tentative (perhaps he will bring news); Naml's less fearful, confident scene uses the definite promise that he will return.
rows.anchor: فبنى الكلام في النمل على القطع {سَآتِيكُمْ} وفي القصص على الترجي {لعلي آتِيكُمْ}

words: وَءَايَةٌ لَّهُمُ ٱلَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ ٱلنَّهَارَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads night as the original whole and daylight as a hide peeled away from it, exposing darkness when the day is removed.
rows.anchor: فجعل النهار كالجلد الذي يُسلخ وأما الليل: فهو الأصل، وهو الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that even if disbelievers were enabled to ascend through a heavenly door, they would end in darkness and claim their vision was clouded.
rows.anchor: لو مكنّاهم من الصعود إلى السماء، لانتهوا إلى ظلام وقالوا: {سُكِّرَتْ أَبْصَارُنَا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic inimitability has linguistic, scientific, historical, psychological, educational, and legal dimensions that continue to be discovered; no person or group in one era can exhaust them.
rows.anchor: فالإعجاز القرآنيّ متعدِّدُ النواحي، متشعب الاتجاهات، ولا يزال الناس يكتشفون من مظاهر إعجازه الشيء الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different specialists can show how a single expression's artistry works from their disciplines, while a linguist identifies its exact word choice, order, and emphasis.
rows.anchor: ويأتيك العالم في الطب ليقول من وجهة نظر الطب
